newsitem.title: UK: Cammell Laird, A&P mull London market flotations.
newsitem.headline: Cammell Laird, A&P mull London market flotations.

text.p: British ship repair and conversion groups A&P Group and Cammell Laird Holdings Plc on Wednesday said they were considering stock market flotations this summer.
Both companies have seen a sharp upturn in profitability in the last year, on the back of a revival in the UK ship repair industry.
A&P's profits jumped last year to about 10 million stg from 3.74 million a year before on sales of 130 million stg.
Cammell, which is expected to be valued at about 20 million stg on flotation, is predicting profits will more than double in the year to April 30 1997 from 700,000 in the previous year.
A&P and Cammell have experienced an increase in demand for their services as ship owners attempt to keep up with advances in marine technology.
Owners have also had to update ships to meet more stringent safety and environmental regulations.

Both companies said a combination of sterling depreciation against the mark over the last five years, lower labour rates and greater flexibility of working practices in the UK had provided them with a competitive edge on rivals in north-west Europe.
Cammell Laird, bought from GEC unit VSEL in 1995 by Coastline Industries, said it hoped to raise up to four million stg of new money.

It said it would use the proceeds to renovate two non-operable dry docks, to improve productivity and efficiency by updating technology used in its repair and conversion facilities, and to expand its technical services division.

Cammell's board of director's includes newly appointed non-executive chairman Juan Kelly, a leading industry figure and an erstwhile Shell International Marine Ltd managing director who had responsibility for the Shell tanker fleet, one of the largest in the world.

A&P Group, which was on the brink of collapse in 1993, has seen its fortunes change for the better after an investment by Schroder Ventures and NatWest Bank, which forced management changes at the ship repairer.
Both Schroder Ventures and NatWest intend to realise their stakeholding and A&P said this could lead to flotation this summer.
A&P, whose highest profile job was on the QE2 liner last year, provides a range of ship repair services and has operations in Falmouth, Southampton and Tyneside.
